title: Banned vanity plate lists from 26 state DMVs and D.C., 2012
hook: In 2012 governmentattic.org asked every state DMV for its list of prohibited personalized plates, and 26 states and D.C. answered. The responses are scans: some are clean lists, some are rejection letters with reason codes, and eleven are only a policy letter. Because every list comes from the same year, the states can be compared with each other directly.
questions: How much of Arkansas's 2012 banned-plate list also appears in Vermont's, and which states built their lists independently?
Which states' 2012 lists ban religious words such as GOD or JESUS, and which ban only profanity?
Which reasons does Utah give most often for a banned plate: sex, drugs, profanity or ethnicity?
notes: Observed 2026-09-12. The dannguyen repo (last commit 2016) holds each state's original PDF, an OCR'd PDF, and an OCR'd xlsx that mixes letter text with the lists. Usable lists: AR, AZ, CO, DC, GA, IA, KS, ME, NJ, NY, OH, OK, UT, VT, WI (NM is short). Letters only, no list: CA, MI, MO, MT, ND, NE, RI, SD, TN, WA, WY. Extract with `pdftotext -layout` on the ocr-pdf files and split columns on two or more spaces, then remove the single spaces OCR puts inside plates ('K N U C K IE'). Each state's layout differs: Utah gives a reason per plate (SEX REFERENCE, DRUG REFERENCE and so on; drop SERIES CONFLICT and ALREADY ISSUED, which are not bans); Colorado's are rejection letters where code 06 means 'possibly offensive'; New York puts a 7-digit id after each plate; Maine's list tags each plate with a state code and is mostly Alaska's (AK ~4,200 of ~6,100), so it is a list assembled from other states' lists. Numbered blocks such as GODS1-GODS32 (GA) and FUBAR2-FUBAR96 (NJ) are ranges, not separate judgements, and inflate any per-theme count. A first pass extracted ~100k state-plate pairs with visible OCR noise.
